investigation.title: Remote Agent Creation Failing: Swarm Agent Quota Exceeded (limit 100) on POST /api/agents
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) are failing with HTTP 409 Conflict on POST /api/agents because the swarm backend reports the agent quota has been exceeded (limit is 100). The eval environment cannot provision a new agent, so no vmId or remoteState evidence is produced, causing all expected-output contract assertions to fail.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm backend is enforcing a hard agent quota of 100 and is rejecting all new agent creation requests with a 409 Conflict error ("conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100"). Because the eval harness creates a fresh agent on each run via POST /api/agents, every check in the remote-agents feature group fails at the creation step before any VM readiness or lifecycle state can be observed. This is a resource-limit exhaustion condition on the swarm layer, not a code defect in the agent creation path itself.
proof: POST /api/agents returned HTTP 409 on all three sibling checks: remote-agent-create (05:12:58Z), remote-agent-state (05:12:59Z), and remote-agent-runtime (05:13:00Z).

Error payload is identical across all three failures: {"error":"swarm agent already exists: {\"error\":{\"code\":\"conflict\",\"message\":\"conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100\"}}","code":"conflict","details":null}
The inner swarm error explicitly states 'agent quota exceeded: limit is 100', indicating the swarm-layer quota ceiling has been reached.
All three checks produced empty evidence objects ({}) — no orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState was captured — confirming the failure occurs before any agent lifecycle state is reachable.
Latencies for all three calls are low (992 ms, 1210 ms, 1221 ms), consistent with an immediate quota-rejection response rather than a timeout or infrastructure hang.
The check staleAfterMinutes is 20, meaning this condition has persisted across at least one full eval cycle as of the run timestamp 2026-06-14T05:13:05Z.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] Swarm agent quota (hard limit: 100) is fully consumed by existing agents that have not been cleaned up — either leaked eval agents from prior runs, long-lived production agents, or both.
[Likely] The eval harness does not perform teardown of agents it creates, causing quota to accumulate across repeated eval runs until the ceiling is hit.
[Possible] A prior eval run or deployment event created agents that were never deleted due to a crash, timeout, or missing cleanup step, leaving orphaned agents counted against the quota.
[Less likely] The quota limit of 100 is too low for the current scale of the production environment and needs to be raised at the swarm configuration level.
[Less likely] A quota-enforcement bug in the swarm backend is incorrectly counting agents (e.g., counting soft-deleted or terminated agents as active).

reproductionSteps.label: Attempt to create a new remote agent via the agents API and observe the 409 response
reproductionSteps.details: Expect HTTP 409 with body containing 'agent quota exceeded: limit is 100' if quota is still exhausted.

reproductionSteps.details: Use the swarm management API or admin console to list all agents scoped to the affected org and count how many are in active/non-terminated states. Compare against the limit of 100.

reproductionSteps.details: Filter the agent list for agents created by the eval harness (e.g., by name prefix, tag, or orgId used by the eval) and check their last-active timestamps to identify stale candidates.

reproductionSteps.label: Delete stale or orphaned agents to free quota headroom
reproductionSteps.details: Issue DELETE requests for confirmed stale agents, then re-run the eval to verify POST /api/agents returns 2xx and evidence fields (vmIdPresent, remoteState) are populated.

reproductionSteps.details: Confirm remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime all return passing status with non-empty evidence including vmIdPresent=true and remoteState in [running, idle, ready].

investigation.title: Remote Agents Eval Failure: Agent Quota Exceeded (HTTP 409 Conflict) Blocking All Remote Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed simultaneously at 2026-06-14T05:12–05:13Z with identical HTTP 409 responses indicating the swarm agent quota of 100 has been reached. Because agent creation is a prerequisite for state polling and runtime checks, the quota exhaustion cascades into a total failure of the remote-agents eval suite.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm backend rejected POST /api/agents with a 409 Conflict carrying the message "agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". The eval harness attempts to create a new agent as its first step; because that creation is blocked by the quota ceiling, no agentId is returned, and all downstream checks (state polling, runtime readiness) cannot proceed. The root cause is that the swarm-level agent quota for the target environment/org has been exhausted, preventing any new agent provisioning.
proof: All three sibling checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) returned HTTP 409 with the identical error body: {"error":"swarm agent already exists: {\"error\":{\"code\":\"conflict\",\"message\":\"conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100\"}}","code":"conflict","details":null}
The error message explicitly states 'agent quota exceeded: limit is 100', confirming the swarm backend has a hard cap of 100 agents and that cap is currently met or exceeded.
Failures occurred within a ~2-second window (05:12:58Z–05:13:00Z), ruling out transient network issues and pointing to a persistent quota state.
The expectedOutputContract requires orgId, agentId, readyState, and state — none of which can be populated because agent creation failed before any of these values could be obtained.
Latency for all three failing calls was under 1.3 seconds (992ms, 1210ms, 1221ms), consistent with an immediate quota-rejection at the API layer rather than a timeout or infrastructure failure.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] The eval environment's org or swarm namespace has accumulated 100 live agents (possibly from prior eval runs that did not clean up after themselves), hitting the hard quota limit and blocking all new provisioning.
[Likely] The eval harness does not perform agent teardown/cleanup after each run, causing agents to accumulate across runs until the quota is exhausted.
[Possible] A separate workload or automated process in the same org/swarm namespace provisioned agents concurrently, consuming quota that the eval harness expected to be available.
[Less likely] The quota limit of 100 is misconfigured or too low for the volume of eval runs executed against this environment, causing quota exhaustion under normal eval cadence.

reproductionSteps.label: Query current agent count in the target org/swarm namespace
reproductionSteps.command: GET /api/agents?limit=100 (or equivalent list endpoint) and count active agents to confirm the quota ceiling is reached
reproductionSteps.details: Confirm that the number of existing agents equals or exceeds 100 in the org/namespace used by the eval harness.

reproductionSteps.command: POST /api/agents with the same payload used by the eval harness
reproductionSteps.details: Expect HTTP 409 with error code 'conflict' and message 'agent quota exceeded: limit is 100' if quota is still exhausted.

reproductionSteps.label: Inspect eval harness teardown logic
reproductionSteps.details: Review the eval run lifecycle to determine whether agents created during previous eval runs are being deleted after each run completes. Look for any DELETE /api/agents/{agentId} calls in the harness teardown phase.

reproductionSteps.label: Identify stale/orphaned agents in the namespace
reproductionSteps.command: GET /api/agents (list all) and filter for agents created by the eval harness (e.g., by name prefix or label)
reproductionSteps.details: Determine how many agents were created by prior eval runs and never cleaned up.

reproductionSteps.label: Manually delete orphaned eval agents to restore quota headroom
reproductionSteps.command: DELETE /api/agents/{agentId} for each orphaned eval agent identified in the previous step
reproductionSteps.details: After deletion, re-run the eval suite to confirm the 409 is resolved and all three checks pass.

investigation.title: Remote Agents Eval Failure: Agent Quota Exceeded (HTTP 409 Conflict) Blocking All Remote-Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed simultaneously at 2026-06-14T05:12:58–05:13:00Z with identical HTTP 409 responses indicating the swarm agent quota of 100 has been reached. The eval cannot provision a new agent to complete its runtime assertion, so the expected-output contract (requiring a "hello from aura" message) was never reachable.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm backend is returning a hard quota-exceeded conflict ("agent quota exceeded: limit is 100") on POST /api/agents. Because the eval lifecycle depends on successfully creating a new agent before it can test VM readiness, lifecycle state, and chat readiness, the quota ceiling is blocking the very first step of every check in the remote-agents feature. This is an eval-blocking infrastructure/quota condition, not a code regression in the agent runtime itself; there is no evidence of a user-traffic or production outage beyond the eval's inability to provision its test agent.
proof: All three sibling checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) returned HTTP 409 with body: {"error":"swarm agent already exists: {\"error\":{\"code\":\"conflict\",\"message\":\"conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100\"}}","code":"conflict","details":null}

Failures are temporally co-located: remote-agent-create ended at 05:12:58.211Z, remote-agent-state at 05:12:59.203Z, remote-agent-runtime at 05:13:00.424Z — all within a 2-second window, consistent with a single quota-exhaustion condition rather than independent faults.

Latencies for all three checks (1210 ms, 992 ms, 1221 ms) are well below the warning threshold (20000 ms) and outage threshold (60000 ms), confirming the requests reached the swarm API and were rejected immediately — not timed out or dropped.

The expected-output contract requires evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) and an assertion that message contains 'hello from aura'; none of these could be populated because agent creation was rejected before any runtime interaction occurred.

The error message 'swarm agent already exists' combined with 'agent quota exceeded: limit is 100' indicates the quota is exhausted by pre-existing agents, not by a duplicate-creation race within this eval run.
possibleCauses: [Highest confidence] The swarm environment used by the eval has accumulated 100 agents (the hard limit) from prior eval runs, manual tests, or leaked agents that were never cleaned up, leaving no capacity for the eval to create a new agent.
[Medium confidence] A previous eval run crashed or was interrupted after agent creation but before the teardown/cleanup step, leaving orphaned agents that count against the quota.
[Medium confidence] The eval does not perform pre-run cleanup of agents it previously created, so repeated eval executions accumulate agents over time until the quota is hit.
[Lower confidence] The quota limit of 100 is shared across multiple eval environments or tenants, and concurrent usage from another process exhausted the remaining capacity just before this run.

[Lower confidence] The swarm API's conflict detection is incorrectly treating a new agent creation as a duplicate of an existing agent due to a naming or ID collision, surfacing the quota error as a secondary message rather than the primary cause.

followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that queries GET /api/agents and asserts the current agent count is below a safe threshold (e.g., < 90 of 100), alerting before quota exhaustion blocks other checks.
Add a post-run teardown verification eval that confirms the agent created during a run is successfully deleted after the run completes, catching cleanup failures early.

Add a quota headroom check as a required pre-condition gate for the remote-agent-create check, so downstream checks (remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) are skipped with a clear dependency-failure reason rather than all failing independently with the same error.
Introduce a canary eval that creates and immediately deletes an agent on a short interval (e.g., every 5 minutes) to detect quota saturation trends before they cause full check failures.

investigation.title: Image Generation Stream Fails with SESSION_OPEN_FAILED (404) — Agent Runtime Harness Unreachable
investigation.summary: The image generation stream eval failed immediately after `generation_start` because the agent runtime returned a 404, emitting a `SESSION_OPEN_FAILED` error frame and never producing the required `generation_completed` frame or an artifact URL. The harness is either not deployed, misconfigured via `LOCAL_HARNESS_URL` / `SWARM_BASE_URL`, or running an incompatible version that does not expose the expected session endpoint.
investigation.rootCause: The agent runtime harness returned HTTP 404 when the image generation stream attempted to open a session. This caused the stream to terminate at the `SESSION_OPEN_FAILED` error frame, preventing any progress frames or completion payload from being emitted. The root cause is a missing, misconfigured, or version-incompatible harness deployment reachable at the configured `LOCAL_HARNESS_URL` or `SWARM_BASE_URL`. No user-traffic or production incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; impact is scoped to this eval run.
proof: failedCheck.status = 'fail' with message: 'agent runtime endpoint not found (404)'
Stream frame sequence: generation_start → generation_error (SESSION_OPEN_FAILED) → empty message frame. No generation_progress or generation_completed frames were emitted.
failedCheck.evidence.frames[1].data.code = 'SESSION_OPEN_FAILED'

failedCheck.evidence.frames[1].data.message explicitly states: 'the harness is unreachable or running an incompatible version. Verify the harness deployment and the LOCAL_HARNESS_URL / SWARM_BASE_URL configuration.'
Missing required evidence: frameTypes and imageUrlPresent — neither was collected because the stream never progressed past session open.
Eval latency was 2008 ms, well under the warning threshold of 180000 ms, confirming the failure was an immediate hard error, not a timeout.
possibleCauses: [Highest confidence] The harness process is not running or was never deployed in the target environment, causing the session-open HTTP request to resolve to a 404 at the configured base URL.
[High confidence] LOCAL_HARNESS_URL or SWARM_BASE_URL is misconfigured (wrong host, port, or path prefix), pointing the eval harness at a server that does not host the agent runtime endpoint.

[Medium confidence] The harness is deployed but is running an incompatible/older version that does not expose the session-open route expected by the current eval client, resulting in a 404 on that specific path.
[Lower confidence] A network or routing layer (reverse proxy, load balancer, service mesh) is stripping or misrouting the request before it reaches the harness, returning a synthetic 404.
[Lower confidence] The harness was recently redeployed and is still in a startup/initialization state, transiently returning 404 on the session endpoint.

investigations.title: Image Generation Stream Fails with SESSION_OPEN_FAILED (404) — Agent Runtime Harness Unreachable
investigations.summary: The image generation stream eval failed immediately after `generation_start` because the agent runtime returned a 404, emitting a `SESSION_OPEN_FAILED` error frame and never producing the required `generation_completed` frame or an artifact URL. The harness is either not deployed, misconfigured via `LOCAL_HARNESS_URL` / `SWARM_BASE_URL`, or running an incompatible version that does not expose the expected session endpoint.
investigations.rootCause: The agent runtime harness returned HTTP 404 when the image generation stream attempted to open a session. This caused the stream to terminate at the `SESSION_OPEN_FAILED` error frame, preventing any progress frames or completion payload from being emitted. The root cause is a missing, misconfigured, or version-incompatible harness deployment reachable at the configured `LOCAL_HARNESS_URL` or `SWARM_BASE_URL`. No user-traffic or production incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; impact is scoped to this eval run.
proof: failedCheck.status = 'fail' with message: 'agent runtime endpoint not found (404)'
Stream frame sequence: generation_start → generation_error (SESSION_OPEN_FAILED) → empty message frame. No generation_progress or generation_completed frames were emitted.
failedCheck.evidence.frames[1].data.code = 'SESSION_OPEN_FAILED'

failedCheck.evidence.frames[1].data.message explicitly states: 'the harness is unreachable or running an incompatible version. Verify the harness deployment and the LOCAL_HARNESS_URL / SWARM_BASE_URL configuration.'
Missing required evidence: frameTypes and imageUrlPresent — neither was collected because the stream never progressed past session open.
Eval latency was 2008 ms, well under the warning threshold of 180000 ms, confirming the failure was an immediate hard error, not a timeout.
possibleCauses: [Highest confidence] The harness process is not running or was never deployed in the target environment, causing the session-open HTTP request to resolve to a 404 at the configured base URL.
[High confidence] LOCAL_HARNESS_URL or SWARM_BASE_URL is misconfigured (wrong host, port, or path prefix), pointing the eval harness at a server that does not host the agent runtime endpoint.

[Medium confidence] The harness is deployed but is running an incompatible/older version that does not expose the session-open route expected by the current eval client, resulting in a 404 on that specific path.
[Lower confidence] A network or routing layer (reverse proxy, load balancer, service mesh) is stripping or misrouting the request before it reaches the harness, returning a synthetic 404.
[Lower confidence] The harness was recently redeployed and is still in a startup/initialization state, transiently returning 404 on the session endpoint.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Creation Failing: Swarm Agent Quota Exceeded (limit 100) on POST /api/agents
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) are failing with HTTP 409 Conflict on POST /api/agents because the swarm backend reports the agent quota has been exceeded (limit is 100). The eval environment cannot provision a new agent, so no vmId or remoteState evidence is produced, causing all expected-output contract assertions to fail.
investigations.rootCause: The swarm backend is enforcing a hard agent quota of 100 and is rejecting all new agent creation requests with a 409 Conflict error ("conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100"). Because the eval harness creates a fresh agent on each run via POST /api/agents, every check in the remote-agents feature group fails at the creation step before any VM readiness or lifecycle state can be observed. This is a resource-limit exhaustion condition on the swarm layer, not a code defect in the agent creation path itself.
proof: POST /api/agents returned HTTP 409 on all three sibling checks: remote-agent-create (05:12:58Z), remote-agent-state (05:12:59Z), and remote-agent-runtime (05:13:00Z).

Error payload is identical across all three failures: {"error":"swarm agent already exists: {\"error\":{\"code\":\"conflict\",\"message\":\"conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100\"}}","code":"conflict","details":null}
The inner swarm error explicitly states 'agent quota exceeded: limit is 100', indicating the swarm-layer quota ceiling has been reached.
All three checks produced empty evidence objects ({}) — no orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState was captured — confirming the failure occurs before any agent lifecycle state is reachable.
Latencies for all three calls are low (992 ms, 1210 ms, 1221 ms), consistent with an immediate quota-rejection response rather than a timeout or infrastructure hang.
The check staleAfterMinutes is 20, meaning this condition has persisted across at least one full eval cycle as of the run timestamp 2026-06-14T05:13:05Z.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] Swarm agent quota (hard limit: 100) is fully consumed by existing agents that have not been cleaned up — either leaked eval agents from prior runs, long-lived production agents, or both.
[Likely] The eval harness does not perform teardown of agents it creates, causing quota to accumulate across repeated eval runs until the ceiling is hit.
[Possible] A prior eval run or deployment event created agents that were never deleted due to a crash, timeout, or missing cleanup step, leaving orphaned agents counted against the quota.
[Less likely] The quota limit of 100 is too low for the current scale of the production environment and needs to be raised at the swarm configuration level.
[Less likely] A quota-enforcement bug in the swarm backend is incorrectly counting agents (e.g., counting soft-deleted or terminated agents as active).

reproductionSteps.details: Filter the agent list for agents created by the eval harness (e.g., by name prefix, tag, or orgId used by the eval) and check their last-active timestamps to identify stale candidates.

reproductionSteps.details: Issue DELETE requests for confirmed stale agents, then re-run the eval to verify POST /api/agents returns 2xx and evidence fields (vmIdPresent, remoteState) are populated.
